scenes.title: 01 · Calculus Atelier
scenes.text: Welcome to Calculus Atelier, an adaptive mathematics learning workspace. The system brings together calculus practice, mathematical answer validation, source-linked feedback, and learning analytics. Let us follow a student's learning journey, from choosing an exercise to reviewing progress and planning the next step.

scenes.title: 02 · A personal learning workspace
scenes.text: The student signs in to access a personal learning workspace. Their exercise history and progress are associated with this account, so each new submission contributes to a continuous learning record. The academic interface keeps problem configuration, practice, and feedback within one focused environment.

scenes.title: 03 · Focused calculus practice
scenes.text: The student chooses derivatives and differentiation, then selects a multiple-choice exercise. Topic, difficulty, and question format provide control over the practice session. Behind the interface, course material is retrieved and the mathematical structure of the question is checked before it reaches the learner.

scenes.title: 04 · Learning from an incorrect answer
scenes.text: Here, the student selects an incorrect option. The selected answer remains visible, making the submitted choice easy to review. Mentor feedback presents the result, while the server saves the attempt. This connects immediate feedback with the student's longer-term learning record.

scenes.title: 05 · Feedback with traceable sources
scenes.text: The student opens a course citation directly from the feedback. The source panel shows the relevant chain-rule material, along with its version and source information. Instead of leaving the learner with an unexplained result, the interface provides a clear route back to the underlying course concept.

scenes.title: 06 · Mathematical equivalence
scenes.text: Next, the student switches to a calculation exercise and submits an expanded derivative. Mathematical validation accepts an equivalent expression rather than requiring an exact text match. The correct result is displayed, and this second attempt is saved to the same learning record.

scenes.title: 07 · Academic progress at a glance
scenes.text: The Academic Progress Report brings the student's work into one view. A six-domain radar chart provides an overview, while topic-level details reveal differences in performance. The two exercises just completed are now reflected in the record, connecting individual practice with the broader picture.

scenes.title: 08 · Choosing the next learning step
scenes.text: Further down, the learning brief highlights areas that deserve attention. Topic records and observed concept attempts give context to the recommendation. This helps the student move beyond simply counting completed questions and make a more informed decision about what to practise next.

scenes.title: 09 · A searchable course library
scenes.text: The Course Library provides another route into the learning material. The student filters by applications of derivatives and searches for marginal cost. Hybrid retrieval finds the relevant course note, linking the mathematical idea of a derivative to an applied interpretation of changing cost.

scenes.title: 10 · The Agent Laboratory
scenes.text: The Agent Laboratory exposes the content-production workflow. The student selects a topic and starts a synthesis task. Role messages make the sequence of curation, question construction, scaffolding, and review visible. The result panel confirms completion and shows the saved problem count.

scenes.title: 11 · One connected learning journey
scenes.text: Calculus Atelier connects practice, validation, feedback, course evidence, and progress tracking in one learning journey. Students can work through a question, understand the relevant concept, and use their learning record to guide the next session. Thank you for watching this project demonstration.
